title: Crescendo Club members and having no ally
summary: Rasch lists living members; Johnson says he had to do it all himself because the others were only followers.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Right. You know, there are four living members of your Crescendo Club.
There's you, and there's Walter Bishop and Claude Hopkins and Count Basie.
Oh, he was in there too -- wonderful. I think we heard from him. He asked to be on your committee, and Claude Walter, oh, yeah, right.
Yeah, Fred Norman was back there.
Uh-huh. Now, who was your biggest -- when you formed the Crescendo Club, who was your biggest ally, I mean the one that kind of, you know, buffed you up?

The one that -- you know, when you're doing something, when you want to get together and you get another person, you catch fire with another person, you know, that believes in what you believe, to give you the incentive, you know, to move ahead, who was -- who was the person, would you think, that, if you could recall who was really like your right hand man?
You had to do it yourself?
Do it all yourself or forget it.
That's right. That's the way they were.
They weren't cooperative at all. They were just followers.
If you had enough guts to get them to follow, you were okay.
